sentences.text:
1) The petitioner is seeking bail in a case arising out of FIR No.27/2022 for offences under Section 376 IPC and 7/8 POCSO Act registered with Police Station, Soura, which is stated to be pending trial before the Court of Presiding Officer Fast Track for POCSO Cases, Srinagar (hereinafter referred to as "the trial court").
2) The facts leading to the filing of this petition are that on 31.03.2022, PW Mohammad Amin Mirchal lodged a report with the police alleging therein that he along with his family is residing as a tenant in a house belonging to Vicharnag Trust.

entities.text: Court of Presiding Officer Fast Track for POCSO Cases, Srinagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: On the said day he was told by his wife that in the afternoon while his two minor daughters were playing in the lawn of the house, the petitioner, who also resides along with his family in the same building on the ground floor, called his two minor daughters to his room and gave some money to his elder daughter PW Ruqaya.
The petitioner is alleged to have asked PW Ruqaya to buy some chewing gum for him.
Taking undue advantage of the situation, the petitioner sexually assaulted his minor daughter and tried to rape her.
3) On the basis of aforesaid report, the police registered the FIR and started investigation of the case.
During investigation, the prosecutrix, who is a minor girl of six years age, was subjected to medical examination and her statement under Section 164 of Cr. P. C was recorded.
In her statement she deposed that on the date of the occurrence, she along with her elder sister were playing in the compound of their rented accommodation.
The petitioner sent her elder sister to purchase chewing gum from the market and he asked her to come inside his home.

She further stated that the petitioner brought a kitchen knife and threatened to kill her, whereafter he took off Amit Ambardar vs Union Territory Of J&K on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164690667/
1 her trousers.

entities.text: Amit Ambardar vs Union Territory Of J&K
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner made her to take off her trousers and caught hold of her hand.
She further stated that the petitioner touched her with his hands and started fiddling with her.
She also stated that the petitioner was having some dirty liquid on his hand.
In the meanwhile her mother came over there and she scolded the petitioner.
In the evening her father came and she was taken to the police station whereafter the petitioner was sent to jail.
She further stated that she was taken to a doctor.
She went on to state that the petitioner touched her private part with his hand.
4) After completing investigation of the case, challan was laid before the trial court and the petitioner was booked for offences under Section 376-AB IPC and 7/8 POCSO Act.
5) It appears that the trial court vide its order dated 27.06.2022 has framed charges for offences under Section 506 IPC and Section 10 read with Section 9 of POCSO Act against the petitioner.
It also appears that during trial of the case, the statements of as many as seven witnesses have already been recorded by the trial court.
These include the prosecutrix as well as her parents.
6) It also appears that the petitioner had moved the trial court for grant of bail, firstly on 13.05.2022 and thereafter on 16.06.2023.
The first bail application was dismissed by the learned trial court on 04.03.2023 whereas second one has been dismissed by the trial court on 18.07.2023.

7) The petitioner has sought bail on the grounds that both the parents of the prosecutrix have turned hostile and they have not supported the prosecution case, therefore, he is entitled to grant of bail.

It has been further contended that merely because the prosecutrix has supported the version of the prosecution, the bail application of the petitioner cannot be dismissed because it is unsafe to rely upon the statement of the prosecutrix who is aged only six years.

It has also been contended that the petitioner is in custody for the last more than two years and the minimum punishment prescribed for the offence with which he has been charged is five years imprisonment and, as such, his further incarceration during the trial of the case would not be justified.

It has been further contended that the prosecutrix as well as her parents stand already examined as witnesses by the trial court,
therefore, there is no apprehension of the petitioner influencing the prosecution witnesses, if he is enlarged on bail.
Lastly, it has been submitted that the petitioner is ready to adhere to all the conditions that may be imposed by this Court upon him in case he is released on bail.
8) The bail application has been resisted by the respondents by filing their reply thereto.

In the reply, after narrating the version of the prosecution, it has been contended that the petitioner has committed a heinous offence upon the prosecutrix who is a minor girl of six years age, therefore, he does not deserve to be enlarged on bail.
It has been further contended that in case the petitioner is admitted to bail at this stage, he will threaten the prosecution witnesses who are yet to examined.
9) I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the material on record.
10) Before proceeding to analyze the rival submissions, it is necessary to restate the settled legal position about the matters to be considered for deciding an application for bail.

sentences.text: Section 31 of the said Act makes the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure applicable to the proceedings before a Special Court and it provides that the provisions of the aforesaid Code including the provisions as to bail and bonds shall apply to the proceedings before a Special Court.
It further provides that the Special Court shall be deemed to be a Court of Sessions.
Thus, it is clear that the provisions of Cr. P. C including the provisions as to grant of bail are applicable to the proceedings in respect of offences under the POSCO Act.
The present application is, therefore, required to be dealt with by this Court in accordance with the provisions contained in Section 439 Cr. P. C.

The other provisions of the POCSO Act, which are also required to be kept in mind, are Sections 29 and 30, which read "29. Presumption as to certain offences - Where a person is prosecuted for committing or abetting or attempting to commit any offence under Sections 3, 5, 7 and Section 9 of this Act, the Special Court shall presume, that such person has committed or abetted or attempted to commit the offence, as the case may be unless the contrary is proved."
30. Presumption of

culpable mental state.-(1) In any prosecution for any offence under this Act which requires a culpable mental state on the part of the accused, the Special Court shall presume the existence of such mental stage but it shall be a defence for the accused to prove the fact that hehad no such mental state with respect to the act charged as anoffence in that prosecution.

(2) For the purposes of this Section, a fact is said to be provedonly when the Special Court believes it to exist beyond reasonable doubt and not merely when its existence is established by a preponderance of probability".

12) Section 29 quoted above raises a presumption of commission of an offence under Sections 3, 5, 7 and 9 of the POCSO Act against a person who is prosecuted for commission of the said offence,
unless contrary is proved.

Similarly, Section 30 quoted above raises a presumption with regard to existence of culpable mental state against an accused in prosecution of any offence under the Act which requires a culpable mental state on the part of the accused.
Again, the accused in such a case has been given a right to prove the fact that he had no such mental state.
13) In the light of the aforesaid legal position, let us now analyze the facts of the present case.

In the present case the petitioner is alleged to have committed aggravated sexual assault on the victim who Amit Ambardar vs Union Territory Of J&K on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164690667/
3 is aged only six years.

sentences.text: It is true that maximum punishment prescribed for offence under Section 9 punishable under Section 10 of the POCSO Act is seven years but that is only one of the considerations for grant of bail.

The other considerations like nature of offence, the position of the accused with reference to the victim and the witnesses and the public interest are some of the other considerations which are also required to be taken into account while considering the bail plea of an accused.

14) In the instant case, prima facie, it appears that the victim while making her statement before the trial court during trial of the case has not deviated from the version of occurrence which she narrated in her statement under Section 164 of the Cr. P. C.

It is true that parents of the victim have not supported the prosecution version while making their statements before the trial court during trial of the case but then besides the statement of the victim, the medical opinion of the doctor, the DNA profiling report which has been substantiated by the statements of the doctor and DNA Expert of FSL, Srinagar, whose statements have been recorded during trial of the case, prima facie, support the version of occurrence given by the victim in her statement.

In the face of this material on record,
it cannot be stated that at least until this stage that the petitioner has been able to rebut the presumption that has been triggered against him under Section 29 of the POCSO Act.

15) So far as the contention of the petitioner that most of the material witnesses have been examined by the prosecution during trial of the case and, as such, there is no apprehension of the petitioner influencing the prosecution witnesses, is concerned, the same is contrary to the record.
One of the most material witnesses for the prosecution is the elder sister of the victim, PW Ruqaya, who at the relevant time was only aged nine years.
Her statement is yet to be recorded by the trial court.
Therefore, if at this stage, the petitioner is granted bail, having regard to the tender age of PW Ruqaya, it cannot be ruled out that she would be pressurized by the petitioner.
This apprehension gets strengthened from the fact that the parents of the victim have already resiled from the prosecution version.
16) There is yet another aspect of the matter which disentitles the petitioner from the grant of concession of bail at this stage.
The petitioner is aged about 41 years, as is clear from the title of the petition whereas the victim, at the relevant time, was only six years old.
The petitioner was living in the same building in which the victim along with her family was living and she would call him as her uncle.
There was fiduciary relationship between the petitioner and the victim, who would repose trust and confidence in him being her neighbourer.

By indulging in abhorrent behaviour with the child victim, the petitioner has shaken this trust and confidence and brought bad name to the relationship of a child with her neighbourer who is as good as her father.
S o , i t is not an ordinary offence where an accused has tried to molest a major woman having no acquaintance with her.
It is a case where the petitioner has committed sexual assault upon a girl child who is about 1/6th of his age.
The gap in age of the petitioner and the victim makes his alleged act more heinous and it shows an element of perversion in the offence alleged.
The position of the petitioner qua the victim makes the offence more heinous.
17) In view of the foregoing reasons, I do not find it a fit case where the petitioner should be enlarged on bail, at least till such time the statement of PW Ruqaya is recorded by the trial court.

sentences.text: The application is, therefore, dismissed.

It is, however, directed that the trial court shall expedite the trial of the case and record statements of the remaining prosecution witnesses at the earliest,
preferably within a period of three months from the date a copy of this order is received by the said court.
18) The observations made hereinabove shall remain confined to the decision of the instant application only and shall not be construed as expression of an opinion on the merits of the case.
19) A copy of this order be sent to the learned trial court for information and compliance.
( SANJAY DHAR) JUDGE Srinagar, 14.08.2024 "Bhat Altaf-Secy"
